newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Dragonair's listing plan hits snags - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dragonair's listing plan hits snags - paper.

text.p: The planned initial public offering (IPO) by Hong Kong Dragon Airlines (Dragonair) was being obstructed by disagreements over its post-listing shareholder structure, the Hong Kong Economic Journal said.
Fears of conflicts of interest with its major shareholder China National Aviation Corp (CNAC) also complicated the issue, the paper reported on Thursday.
The IPO of the Hong Kong carrier was expected to be postponed until the end of 1997, the newspaper said. The listing was originally planned for early next year.

The Hong Kong Economic Journal said CITIC Pacific Ltd's unwillingness to see its 28.5 percent stake in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines heavily diluted after the flotation was impeding the listing preparations.
CITIC Pacific declined to comment on the newspaper report.

CNAC, the commercial arm of China's aviation regulator, declined to make any committment to abandon its application for an air operator's certificate in Hong Kong of its own, which further complicated the issue, the newspaper said.
The stock exchange could consider a company unsuitable for listing if the controlling shareholder was operating another firm which was directly competing with the applicant, it said.

It quoted informed sources as saying arrangers of the Dragonair flotation had discussed the implications of this with CNAC, but the company had not promised to abandon the air license application and was unwilling to make a promise to do so in the listing prospectus.

CNAC holds a 36 percent stake in Dragonair and its chairman Wang Guixiang is also the chairman of Dragonair. The Hong Kong Economic Journal said CNAC intends to keep at least a 35 percent stake in the company but was unwilling to pay for new shares.

The Chinese company expected CITIC Pacific and Cathay Pacific Airways, which has a total of 25.5 percent in Dragonair together with its parent Swire Pacific Ltd, to place part of their existing shares in the flotation.
Although Cathay agreed in principle, CITIC Pacific seemed disagree, the newspaper said.
A Cathay Pacific spokesman reiterated Dragonair's intentions to list as soon as practicable but declined to comment on the newspaper report.
CNAC officials were not immediately available for comment.
Market sources have suggested that SBC Warburg, Peregrine Capital and HSBC Investment were joint sponsors of the issue and that BZW Asia was also involved.
